note: Attacker-controlled instruction bytes from the input file are assembled into the 32-bit TMS320C64x instruction word; the all-zero word used here decodes as a NOP.

code: result = decodeInstruction_4(DecoderTable32, MI, insn, address, info, 0);
note: DecoderTable32 matches the zero word (Inst{6-2}=0, Inst{11-7}=0, bit 12=0, bits 27-17=0) to the NOP_n entry, setting internal opcode 162 and an NOP immediate of 1.
TMS320C64x_get_insn_id maps the internal NOP_n opcode to the public instruction ID TMS320C64X_INS_NOP (enum value 83), which is stored in insn->id.
The public instruction ID (83) is forwarded from the generic API to the architecture-specific name lookup function TMS320C64x_insn_name.

Root cause: the bounds check validates id only against the enum sentinel TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING (145) instead of the actual size of insn_name_maps (ARR_SIZE == 3), so every valid public ID in [3, 145) passes this check.
Sink: insn_name_maps is a 3-element global array but id==83 is used to index it, causing a global-buffer-overflow read past the array.
